rows.grounds: compound denoting modes of death: śastra (weapon), agni (fire), bhṛgupāta (fall from a height), ambupraveśa (entry into water)
instrumental indicating the manner or prescribed procedure
past participle referring to those who have died

items.question: Which modes of death qualify individuals for inclusion in the prescribed ancestral rites?
premises: Death may occur by weapon, fire, falling from a height, or entering water.
Such deaths are considered in relation to a prescribed rite.
Individuals who have died in these specified ways are identified as a distinct group.
items.inference: Those who died by weapon, fire, falling from a height, or entering water according to the prescribed rite constitute a category designated for ancestral rites.
uncertainties: Whether vidhinā qualifies the manner of death or the ritual procedure applied to the deceased is contextually ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Those who have died by weapon, fire, falling from a height, or entering water according to the prescribed rite.
